questions.stem: Convert to Indirect Speech: Rama said, 'I am going to school.'

options.option_text: Rama said that he is going to school. (wrong: 'is going' → past tense needed in indirect speech if reporting verb is past)
Rama said that he was going to school. (correct: 'said' is past; 'am going' → 'was going'; 'I' → 'he' ✓)
Rama said that I was going to school. (wrong: pronoun 'I' must change to 'he' in indirect speech)
Rama said that he had gone to school. (wrong: 'was going' becomes 'had gone' only for past continuous → past perfect; here it's present continuous → past continuous)

questions.explanation: B is correct. RULES for indirect speech: (1) Remove inverted commas; add 'that'. (2) Change pronouns: I → he/she. (3) Tense backshift (when reporting verb is past): am/is/are → was/were; am going → was going. Direct: 'I am going' → Indirect: 'he was going to school'.

questions.stem: Convert to Indirect Speech: She said to me, 'You have done a great job.'

options.option_text: She told me that you have done a great job. (wrong: 'you' must change to 'I'; also tense backshift needed)
She told me that I had done a great job. (correct: 'said to me' → 'told me'; 'you' → 'I'; 'have done' → 'had done' ✓)
She said me that I had done a great job. (wrong: 'said me' is incorrect; should be 'told me' when a person is mentioned)
She told me that I have done a great job. (wrong: tense must backshift; 'have done' → 'had done')

questions.explanation: B is correct. Key changes: (1) 'said to me' → 'told me' (when an object is mentioned, 'said to' becomes 'told'). (2) Pronoun 'you' (referring to speaker's partner = 'me') → 'I'. (3) Tense backshift: 'have done' (present perfect) → 'had done' (past perfect).

questions.stem: Convert to Indirect Speech: He said, 'The sun rises in the east.'

options.option_text: He said that the sun rose in the east. (wrong: universal/scientific truths DON'T backshift tense in indirect speech)
He said that the sun rises in the east. (correct: scientific/permanent truths retain present tense in indirect speech even with past reporting verb ✓)
He said that the sun had risen in the east. (wrong: past perfect is wrong for permanent truth)
He said that the sun was rising in the east. (wrong: present continuous is wrong for a permanent fact)

questions.explanation: B is correct. EXCEPTION: Tense does NOT change for UNIVERSAL/SCIENTIFIC TRUTHS in indirect speech. 'The sun rises in the east' is a permanent fact → tense stays as present simple even when reporting verb is past. Other exceptions: historical facts, mathematical truths.

questions.stem: Convert to Direct Speech: She asked me if I had finished my homework.

options.option_text: She said, 'Did you finish your homework?' (wrong: the indirect speech uses past perfect → direct was past simple; 'had finished' → 'have you finished?' actually)
She said, 'Have you finished your homework?' (correct: 'asked...if' = indirect yes/no question; 'had finished' → 'have finished' (backshift reversed); 'I' → 'you' ✓)
She said, 'You have finished your homework.' (wrong: this is a statement; 'asked if' indicates a question)
She asked, 'Has she finished her homework?' (wrong: wrong pronouns — the question was about the person she was speaking to)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Converting indirect to direct: 'asked...if' → yes/no question with question mark. Reverse tense backshift: 'had finished' → 'have finished'. Pronoun: 'I' → 'you'. 'She asked me IF I had finished' → 'She said, HAVE YOU FINISHED your homework?' (present perfect question).

questions.stem: Convert to Indirect Speech: The teacher said to the students, 'Be quiet.'

options.option_text: The teacher told the students to be quiet. (correct: imperatives in indirect speech use 'told/asked/ordered + object + to + infinitive' ✓)
The teacher said the students that they be quiet. (wrong: 'said the students' is incorrect; also 'that they be quiet' is wrong for imperatives)
The teacher told the students that be quiet. (wrong: 'that be quiet' is incorrect; should be 'to be quiet')
The teacher said to the students to be quiet. (wrong: 'said to' should change to 'told' when a direct object is present)

questions.explanation: A is correct. IMPERATIVE sentences in indirect speech: Remove 'Be/Do/Don't' and use 'told/asked/ordered + object + to + V1'. 'Be quiet' → 'told the students TO BE quiet.' Rule for negative imperatives: 'Don't go' → 'told them NOT TO GO.'

questions.stem: Convert to Indirect Speech: He said, 'I will come tomorrow.'

options.option_text: He said that he would come the next day. (correct: 'will' → 'would'; 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'; 'I' → 'he' ✓)
He said that he will come tomorrow. (wrong: 'will' must change to 'would'; 'tomorrow' must change to 'the next day')
He said that he would come tomorrow. (wrong: 'tomorrow' must change to 'the next day' in indirect speech)
He told that he would come the next day. (wrong: 'told' requires an object — 'He told them/him that...' — 'told that' alone is wrong)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Time/place word changes in indirect speech: tomorrow → the next day; yesterday → the previous day; today → that day; here → there; now → then; this → that; these → those. Tense change: will → would.

questions.stem: Convert to Indirect Speech: She said, 'Can you help me?'

options.option_text: She asked if I could help her. (correct: 'can' → 'could'; 'you' → 'I' (from speaker's viewpoint); 'me' → 'her'; question with 'if' since it's yes/no ✓)
She asked if you can help her. (wrong: 'can' must change to 'could'; 'you' must change)
She said that could I help her. (wrong: 'said that could I' is not grammatical; question becomes 'if + declarative')
She asked that can I help her. (wrong: 'that can' is wrong; should be 'if I could')

questions.explanation: A is correct. Yes/No questions → indirect: 'asked + if/whether + subject + verb'. Question word order becomes declarative. 'Can you help me?' → 'She asked if I COULD HELP HER.' Changes: can → could; you (2nd person) → I; me (speaker = she) → her.

questions.stem: Convert to Indirect Speech: Riya said to Mohan, 'Where do you live?'

options.option_text: Riya asked Mohan where he lived. (correct: Wh-questions → 'asked + wh-word + subject + past verb'; 'do you live' → 'he lived' ✓)
Riya asked Mohan where did he live. (wrong: in indirect speech, question word order is NOT used — use declarative order: 'where he lived', not 'where did he live')
Riya said Mohan where he lived. (wrong: 'said Mohan' is wrong; 'asked Mohan' is correct for questions)
Riya told Mohan where did you live. (wrong: multiple errors — 'told' is for statements; 'did you' reverses the changes)

questions.explanation: A is correct. WH-questions in indirect speech: 'asked + wh-word + subject + verb (declarative order, past tense)'. 'Where do you live?' → 'asked Mohan WHERE HE LIVED.' Key: no 'did' in indirect questions; the auxiliary disappears and verb takes past form. 'Do you live' → 'he lived.'

questions.stem: Which is the correct indirect speech for: 'Please lend me your pen,' said Amit to Priya.

options.option_text: Amit requested Priya to lend him her pen. (correct: 'please' + imperative → 'requested + object + to + V1'; 'me' → 'him'; 'your' → 'her' ✓)
Amit asked Priya please to lend him her pen. (wrong: 'please' is not kept in indirect speech)
Amit told Priya to lend him her pen. (wrong: 'please' indicates a polite request → 'requested', not 'told')
Amit said Priya to lend him her pen. (wrong: 'said' without 'to' object and 'told' without object — both wrong forms)

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Please' in direct speech → 'requested' in indirect speech. 'Told' is for commands; 'ordered' for strict orders; 'requested' for polite please-requests; 'warned' for warnings. 'Me' → 'him' (Amit's perspective); 'your' (Priya's pen) → 'her'.

questions.stem: Convert to Indirect Speech: She exclaimed, 'What a beautiful painting this is!'

options.option_text: She exclaimed with joy that that was a very beautiful painting. (correct: exclamatory → 'exclaimed + that + noun phrase with 'very'; 'this' → 'that' ✓)
She said what a beautiful painting that was. (wrong: exclamatory sentences need 'exclaimed'; also 'what a' is kept in indirect form)
She exclaimed what a beautiful painting that was. (wrong: needs 'that' after 'exclaimed' and must restructure)
She told that painting was beautiful. (wrong: loses the exclamation; 'told' is wrong without an indirect object)

questions.explanation: A is correct. EXCLAMATORY sentences → Indirect: 'exclaimed with joy/surprise/sorrow + that + subject + verb (past) + noun phrase (convert 'What a...' to 'very...')'. 'What a beautiful painting this is!' → 'exclaimed with joy THAT THAT WAS A VERY BEAUTIFUL PAINTING.' 'This' → 'that' (place change).
